rv.q: The material is novel, but not new. There's probably nothing in this story that audiences haven't seen or heard before, but the melodies are so often alluring, and Bryant's lyrics either bite or make us think or provoke a laugh now and then.
It may well be worth seeing this show for the great performances alone (especially Leigh's) despite its issues.
This play has it all. And a good reason to get out of the house and enjoy 90 minutes of true entertainment.

cn.t: This Australian chamber musical earns praise for its exploration of truth and lies, with critics highlighting strong performances and the compelling 75-minute one-act structure that reveals secrets through four characters.
